name: Sky-cooled carbon capture tower
subtitle: a carbon capture tower chilled by night sky

effects.effect: sponge-like crystals with a huge inner surface trap one chosen gas
a surface that reflects sunlight and glows in infrared cools below air temperature in full sun
heat flows only from hot to cold on its own

effect: sponge-like crystals with a huge inner surface trap one chosen gas
how: Machines that pull carbon dioxide out of thin air spend most of their energy swinging a sponge between cold (when it grabs the gas) and hot (when it lets go), and that energy makes the whole business too expensive. Here the sponge is a crystal with a vast inner surface, and the cold half of the swing is free: a roof that reflects sunlight and glows in the infrared colours the sky lets straight through runs below air temperature even in sun, and the hot half comes from a mirror and the day's sunshine. The tower breathes in cold air at night and gives back pure carbon dioxide by day.
obstacle: Sky cooling only buys a handful of degrees, so the roof has to be acres wide per tonne of carbon and stay spotless.
why: Free night cold replaces the costly cooling half of every air-capture cycle.
real: A DOE-funded SUNY-Buffalo project designed exactly this cycle — membrane sorbents regenerated by solar heating and loaded during electricity-free radiative cooling (5-7 C below ambient) — but only as materials work plus preliminary techno-economics, with no working tower demonstrated.
